question: The revolt of 1857 was started by the sepoys from which of the following places?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Meerut**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Revolt of 1857**, also known as India’s First War of Independence, began on **May 10, 1857**, in the town of **Meerut**, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh.

• The revolt was triggered by the grievances of the **sepoys (Indian soldiers)** employed under the British East India Company, particularly due to the introduction of the controversial **Enfield rifle**.

• The new rifle cartridges were rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat, which offended both **Hindus (who consider the cow sacred)** and **Muslims (who regard the pig as unclean)**.

• In Meerut, 85 sepoys of the 3rd Bengal Light Cavalry refused to use the cartridges and were subsequently court-martialed and imprisoned. This act of punishment outraged their comrades and sparked a rebellion.

• On the night of May 10, 1857, the sepoys in Meerut rose in rebellion, broke into the jail to free their comrades, and marched towards **Delhi**, where they declared the Mughal Emperor **Bahadur Shah II** as their leader.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Causes of the Revolt:**

• **Political Causes:** The annexation policies of the British (e.g., the Doctrine of Lapse) alienated many Indian rulers.

• **Economic Causes:** Heavy taxation, the destruction of traditional industries, and the exploitation of resources led to widespread poverty.

• **Social and Religious Causes:** The British imposed reforms and practices that were perceived as an attack on Indian social and religious traditions.

• **Military Causes:** Discrimination in pay, promotion, and treatment of Indian sepoys compared to their British counterparts created resentment.

• **Course of the Revolt:**

• After starting in Meerut, the revolt spread to various parts of northern and central India, including **Delhi, Kanpur, Jhansi, and Lucknow**.

• Key leaders included **Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi**, **Begum Hazrat Mahal of Awadh**, and **Tantia Tope**.

• Despite initial successes, the lack of coordination, resources, and modern weaponry led to the revolt's failure by 1858.

• **Consequences of the Revolt:**

• The British Crown assumed direct control over India, ending the rule of the East India Company.

• The policy of annexation was abandoned, and greater respect was given to Indian customs and traditions.

• Reforms were introduced in the Indian Army to prevent future revolts, including increasing the proportion of British soldiers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Significance of Meerut:** The revolt in Meerut marked the beginning of a widespread anti-colonial movement and was a turning point in Indian history.

• **Delhi’s Role:** The sepoys’ decision to march to Delhi and proclaim Bahadur Shah II as the Emperor of India symbolized a unifying attempt to restore Indian rule.

• **British Response:** The British took about a year to suppress the rebellion, deploying reinforcements and employing brutal measures to crush resistance.

• **Legacy:** Although the revolt failed, it sowed the seeds for future movements for independence, inspiring subsequent generations of freedom fighters.

a7:T
